in your opinion, what is the best 1st episode of a TV series ever?

I don't watch many TV series, but from recent memory:

  • Agents of SHEILD - I wasn't into the first episode because of what I was seeing, but because I was excited for what it was going to be.
  • Arrow - So many things happened in just one episode. I really liked all of the action.
  • Legend of Korra - I was riding the hype train high. I don't even remember the episode.

I'm not a big TV person anymore, but I remember when The Last Airbender came out and I happened to see the first episode. I distinctly remember being in middle school and I couldn't stop watching it. That first episode hooked me and it wasn't even my favorite episode from the series.

I don't know about best first episode ever, but for most impressive reception, Better Call Saul has got to take it. For the high high expectations people had, it seemed like all the BB fans were satisfied. I can't think of a show that stepped into its stride so easily, on the first episode. I'm sure it helps that the setting and some of the characters are already established, but it's a very different show.

Game of Thrones.

First scene itself sets the direction of the whole series and one can't lift the ass from the seat till the episode is over. And when the episode is over, one is left hungry for the second - the twist at the end simply stumps any thinking about where the micro story is heading. Actors, direction, music, costumes and everything technical people can talk about flawlessly fits in. Nothing on TV or elsewhere is as well made for the first watch or as addictive.
The whole "direwolf killed by the stag" in the opening scene leaving the pups orphaned was just the perfect omen to start the series with. It also perfectly illustrated Jon's bastard-ness.

Not only Jon's bastardness, but his sensibleness and his otherwise suitability to be a heroic leader.

The episode gives a good first impression to every character: Ned, Ned's wife, sons, daughters, Baratheon and his family.... The only place the episode deceives is with Lennister brothers. Terion, in particular.

Fuck, now I want to watch that episode again and I know that I can't stop at just one.

Hmm good question, there are two that immediately spring to mind for me:

House of Cards - Immediately hooked by Kevin Spacey breaking the fourth wall.

The Newsroom - First scene, Jeff Daniels ripping on America, I was hooked.

Just watched the first episode of Breaking Bad a few days ago and despite all the hype leading into it -- the episode satisfied on every level. So much happened (and of such a great magnitude) that I remember telling my brother, "This first episode alone could have easily been a week's worth of episodes from any other show."
Hands down, Lost. I was blown away by the first episode. Had me completely hooked.
1st was great, but i left after the 2 season, it just didn't hold me after that.

Oh, I agree entirely. I left about 5 episodes in to Season 2. It was that damned bunker thing. It became pretty obvious to me that the writers were like a kid with a new toy, everything all of a sudden was about the bunker. It was then that I started to realize the writers have no idea where this story is going. I am glad I bailed when I did, as everything I heard afterward about the show supported that idea.

Red Dwarf.

Everyone's doing stuff and after a short period of being kept in a "coma", everyone's dead Dave.

I need to watch it again.

Without a doubt it is the pilot for The Walking Dead (Days Gone By). This episode works as a stand alone zombie movie and an incredible on at that. You can show people that episode and they will be satisfied. They could watch the whole series or not, it doesn't matter. The story in that one episode is as good as any of the best Zombie movies ever made.
I really liked the first episode of Better Call Saul (the new Breaking Bad spin-off). Definitely my personal favorite. Honestly the whole series has been pretty great so far.

Not a fan of this idea for three reasons:

  1. Subs work as a sort of "filters" on topics of discussion. For instance a /physics sub is going to have quite a different perspective on a report of somebody claiming to have accelerated a particle beyond the speed of light than a /news sub would. And even though the /news sub is undoubtedly going to be vastly more popular, I think most of the folks in /physics would prefer to see the submission and comments from /physics by default.

  2. It empowers votes. I see votes on message boards as a sort of necessary evil. They work as yet another filter to try and improve the signal:noise ratio and when points and votes are meaningless, aside from this perk, it is a good thing. However, in spite of this worthlessness we saw on Reddit people would begin to "karma whore" just for the sake of accumulating more points much to the detriment of of their actual and original purpose. Adding an actual competitive aspect to vote counts is probably not going to do great things.

  3. It empowers mods. Again one of the things I think we learned from Reddit is that mods should, in general, be as powerless as possible while still being able to function as a sort of group janitor. Presumably this idea would be opt-in, but even there suddenly you have mods able to bring over content and messages from subs that users of their sub might not actually want. We need to do all we can to ensure that mods are subject to the whims of their community and not vice versa.
